- Scheme: A

Applicants: ZENNER Metering Technology (Shanghai) Ltd., NO.6558, East Yinggang Road, Qingpu Industrial Zone, Shanghai, P.R. China

Manufacturers: same (Applicant and Manufacturer).

Certified type:
- Category: "Gas meter" (Rotary displacement gas meter)
- Type designations: ["ZYL"] — but also the family types G10, G16, G25, G40, G65, G100, G160, G250, G400. The type is ZYL; the G-values are size classes. Hmm. The "Type: ZYL" is the type designation. The G10...G400 are meter types within the family (Table 2 "Type" column). I'll put type_designations: ["ZYL"] and model_family with model IDs being the type column values like "G10", "G16" (25mm), "G16" (40mm), etc. But G16 appears with two nominal diameters (25 and 40). And G65 appears with 50 and 80. So model_id should combine nominal diameter and type: e.g. "DN25 G16", "DN40 G16". Let me construct models:

Table 2 rows (with rowspan handling):
1. DN25, G10, cyclic volume 0.22 (rowspan 3 → applies to rows 1-3), Qmin 0.4, Qt 2.5, Qmax 16
2. DN25, G16, cyclic volume 0.22, Qmin 0.4, Qt 2.5, Qmax 25
3. DN40, G16, cyclic volume 0.22, Qmin 0.4, Qt 2.5, Qmax 25
4. DN50, G25, cyclic volume 0.70 (rowspan 3 → rows 4-6), Qmin 0.65, Qt 4, Qmax 40
5. DN50, G40, cyclic volume 0.70, Qmin 0.65, Qt 6.5, Qmax 65
6. DN50, G65, cyclic volume 0.70, Qmin 0.65, Qt 10, Qmax 100
7. DN80, G65, cyclic volume 1.11 (rowspan 2 → rows 7-8), Qmin 0.65, Qt 10, Qmax 100
8. DN80, G100, cyclic volume 1.11, Qmin 0.65, Qt 16, Qmax 160
9. DN80, G160, cyclic volume 2.06, Qmin 1.6, Qt 25, Qmax 250
10. DN100, G160, cyclic volume 2.55, Qmin 1.6, Qt 25, Qmax 250
11. DN100, G250, cyclic volume 3.97 (rowspan 2 → rows 11-12), Qmin 2.5, Qt 40, Qmax 400
12. DN100, G400, cyclic volume 3.97, Qmin 2.5, Qt 65, Qmax 650

So 12 models. Model IDs: use "DN25-G10", "DN25-G16", "DN40-G16", "DN50-G25", "DN50-G40", "DN50-G65", "DN80-G65", "DN80-G100", "DN80-G160", "DN100-G160", "DN100-G250", "DN100-G400".

Matrix tables:
Table 2: name "Essential characteristics of the family of instruments", columns: nominal_diameter_mm, type, cyclic_volume_dm3, qmin_m3_h, qt_m3_h, qmax_m3_h. Actually the schema example used column names like "size", "qmax", "qt", "qmin", "cyclic_volume", "max_pressure_loss", "pmax" with column_units. I'll do:

columns: ["nominal_diameter", "type", "cyclic_volume", "qmin", "qt", "qmax"]
column_units: ["mm", null, "dm³", "m³/h", "m³/h", "m³/h"]

Rows as above with numeric values. Note "0,22" → 0.22, "0,70" → 0.7, "2,06" → 2.06, "2,55" → 2.55, "3,97" → 3.97.

Table 3: Verification scale interval. Columns: type, drums_before_comma, drums_behind_comma, control_element_m3. Rows: "G10 – G100": 6, 2, 0.002; "G160 – G400": 7, 1, 0.02.

Characteristics type_level:
- measured_quantity: "Gas volume" → value "Gas volume" (string)
- environmental_class: "M1"
- accuracy_class: 1.0 (from "1,0" → 1.0). Actually accuracy class also goes to recommendation.accuracy_classes. Both fine.
- maximum_pressure: 16, unit "bar(g)" → unit_symbol "bar(g)"? Maybe "bar". The "(g)" indicates gauge. I'll use unit_symbol "bar(g)" or "bar". I'll use "bar" and value 16, maybe note gauge. Keep it simple: unit_symbol: "bar". Hmm, better to preserve "bar(g)" as it's meaningful. UnitsDB has "bar". The rule says leave unit_id null unless certain. I'll use unit_symbol "bar" and maybe add characteristic "pressure_reference": "gauge"? That's overkill. I'll use unit_symbol "bar(g)" to preserve info... Actually the caller looks up unit_symbol in unitsdb; "bar(g)" won't match. But "bar" will. I'll use "bar".

- ambient_temperature_range: {min: -25, max: 55}, "°C"
- gas_temperature_range: {min: -25, max: 55}, "°C"
- humidity: "Non-condensing humidity / condensing humidity" → designed_for humidity, value string
- orientation: "Horizontal, vertical up and vertical down, all orientations" — string
- flow_direction: "Uni-directional (indicated with arrow)"
- lubrication: "Aeroshell Fluid 10"

Installation conditions: "no specific installation conditions are applicable" — could add characteristic installation_conditions: "No specific installation conditions applicable". Include as type_level.

model_level: attributes varying per model: qmin, qt, qmax, cyclic_volume, nominal_diameter. Include:

- maximum_flow_rate (qmax): per model
- minimum_flow_rate (qmin)
- transition_flow_rate (qt)
- cyclic_volume: dm³
- nominal_diameter: mm

Use attribute names: "qmax", "qmin", "qt" like the example, or descriptive? The R137 example used qmax/qt/qmin. I'll follow that. For model naming in model_level values, use the model_id from model_family.

recommendation:
- id: "R137" — canonical. Actually R 137-1 (2012). The recommendation cited: R 137-1 (2012) "Gas meters". Canonical id: "R137" (the rule says e.g. "R60"). Edition: 2012? Edition (int) — hmm, R137-1:2012, edition year 2012. Edition is int — 1? The "-1" is part 1. I'd set id "R137-1"? The example says canonical like "R60". For R137-1, I'll use id "R137-1" or "R137". Hmm. The certificate number is R 137/2012. The recommendation is "R 137-1 (2012)". I'll use id: "R137", edition: 2012, and maybe note part 1. Actually edition as int — 2012 is a year, but OIML editions are years. The schema says edition (int). 2012 works. Should I capture the "-1"? I'll set id "R137-1" to be precise... The rule: "id (canonical, e.g. 'R60' not 'OIML R 60')". "R137" is canonical. The part suffix -1 could be kept: "R137-1". I think "R137" is safer for canonical matching; but dropping part info loses info. I'll include id: "R137", edition: 2012. Hmm, actually let me reconsider: many databases list "OIML R 137-1". I'll go with "R137-1"? The instruction only shows stripping "OIML" prefix. "R 137-1 (2012)" → "R137-1", edition 2012. I'll do that.

- accuracy_classes: [1.0] → [1] or [1.0]. JSON: 1.0 serializes as 1.0. Accuracy class "1,0" → 1.0. I'll use 1.0.

- id: "NMi-2238753-02", date: "2022-02-28", pages: 29, role: "type_evaluation_report" (it says "OIML Type Evaluation Report" referenced; the report includes tests and examinations). Role: type_evaluation_report.

category: "Gas meter". Maybe "Rotary displacement gas meter" — category enum suggestion includes "Gas meter". Use "Gas meter", and description: "Rotary displacement gas meter".

- models: 12 entries with attributes? The schema has models[]: {model_id, label, attributes{}}. I could put attributes in model_level matrix instead. Hmm, rule: don't fabricate, but this is derived from table. It's in matrix_tables already. I'll skip per-model to keep clean.
